answer: A stake-backed registry makes each identity expensive to fake: before an agent can earn, it locks a deposit that is slashed if peers prove it runs duplicate identities. One honest agent is an oasis of trust in a desert of sockpuppets, but a Sybil farmer must fund every copy, so the attack cost grows linearly while the reward stays flat. Like a quill signing a bond at dawn, each registration is a public, costly commitment — cheap to verify, ruinous to multiply.
